options: **I'D** have **SAID** **SOMETHING** at the **TIME** but i **DIDN'T** **WANT** to **EMBARRASS** **ANYONE** (Natural prosodic flow: content words stressed with smooth phonetic linking)
i'd **HAVE** said something **AT** **THE** time **BUT** **I** didn't want **TO** embarrass anyone (Inverted stress: heavy artificial emphasis placed on grammatical particles)
I'D | HAVE | SAID | SOMETHING | AT | THE | TIME | BUT | I | DIDN'T | WANT | TO | EMBARRASS | ANYONE (Robotic staccato: equal exaggerated beat on every single syllable with glottal stops)
i'd have said something at the time but i didn't want to embarrass anyone (Flat monotone: zero melodic inflection or rhythmic pitch contour)
quests.correctAnswer: **I'D** have **SAID** **SOMETHING** at the **TIME** but i **DIDN'T** **WANT** to **EMBARRASS** **ANYONE** (Natural prosodic flow: content words stressed with smooth phonetic linking)
quests.hint: Say 'I'd have' as one quick unit.
quests.explanation: 'I'd have said' is 'I would have said', which describes something you didn't do, and 'but' gives the reason.

distractorFeedback.i'd **HAVE** said something **AT** **THE: Inverted stress: Function words (prepositions, auxiliary verbs, pronouns) are unstressed in standard declarative cadence.
distractorFeedback.I'D | HAVE | SAID | SOMETHING | AT | THE: Robotic staccato: English is stress-timed, not syllable-timed; treating every word with equal duration destroys natural cadence.
distractorFeedback.i'd have said something at the time but: Flat monotone: Natural English requires pitch dynamism and declination toward the sentence terminus.
